gse_mapping: State transitions in consumer groups governed by offset commitment logic and partition assignment policies under dynamic load. GSE models partition state transitions via segment lifecycle events (open/close/delete); state-space evolution reflects file handle management and disk I/O constraints, enabling dynamic workload balancing.

primitives.name: Consumer Deserialization Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: The other two properties, key.deserializer and value.deserializer, are similar to the serializers defined for the producer, but rather than specifying classes that turn Java objects to byte arrays, you need to specify classes that can take a byte array and turn it into a Java object.

primitives.name: Offset Commit Logic
primitives.verbatim_quote: Fortunately, the consumer API allows you to call commitSync() and commitAsync() and pass a map of partitions and offsets that you wish to commit.

primitives.name: Active Segment Invariance Principle
primitives.verbatim_quote: The segment we are currently writing to is called an active segment.

primitives.name: Segment File Handle Count Law
primitives.verbatim_quote: As you learned in Chapter 2, a Kafka broker will keep an open file handle to every segment in every partition—even inactive segments.

primitives.assumptions: Each segment requires one file descriptor regardless of activity status.
primitives.breakdown_regime: OS resource exhaustion when H exceeds system limits, leading to broker failure.

layer2.mapping: File handle count law governs kernel-level resource allocation in GSE's I/O scheduler; analogous to memory pressure in neural network training loops.

primitives.name: Message Format Consistency Theorem
primitives.verbatim_quote: The format of the data on the disk is identical to the format of the messages that we send from the producer to the broker and later from the broker to the consumers.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Format mismatch causes deserialization errors during inter-broker communication or consumer processing.

layer2.mapping: Message format consistency enforces protocol equivalence between GSI's data ingestion pipeline and GSE's event processing engine; ensures fidelity across abstraction layers.

primitives.name: Segment Roll Policy Dynamics
primitives.verbatim_quote: If you choose to store data for a week and roll a new segment every day, you will see that every day we will roll a new segment while deleting the oldest segment—so most of the time the partition will have seven segments.
primitives.assumptions: Roll policy is periodic and deterministic with fixed duration intervals.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Excessive segment count when D_{\text{store}} > N_{\text{segments}} * R, causing performance degradation.
